commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG NFRs and glossary for TutorContacts
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide still lists AB3's generic non-functional
requirements and glossary, which do not describe TutorContacts or
the course constraints that apply to it.

Let's replace them with TutorContacts-specific entries:

* Group the NFRs by platform, performance, usability, data and
  reliability, and scope and privacy, drawing on the course
  constraints and the team's MVP specification.
* Make each NFR measurable so that it can be verified.
* Define the domain and UI terms used in the user stories and use
  cases, and drop the unused AB3 term "Private contact detail".

"Normalized name" follows the current implementation: names are
trimmed and compared exactly (case-sensitive).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace AB3 placeholders in AboutUs and DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The AboutUs page and the DG still contain placeholders copied from
AB3: a lecturer's homepage link, johndoe portfolio links, AB3's
contact email, and an empty DG Acknowledgements section. These make
the TutorContacts documentation look unfinished and point readers
to pages unrelated to the team.

Let's remove the placeholder links and email, and acknowledge AB3,
SE-EDU, and the third-party libraries in the DG. Portfolio links are
left out until a member opts into the optional Project Portfolio

Also use https for all GitHub profile links for consistency.

commitResults.messageTitle: Define normalized name to collapse inner spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
The glossary defines a normalized name as trimmed only, but the
agreed MVP specification also collapses consecutive internal spaces
in names, as pointed out in the PR review.

Let's include that rule so the definition matches the specification.
Names are still compared exactly, so capitalization still matters.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command for displayed contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
The MVP specification includes a view command, but TutorContacts
has no way to select one contact from the displayed list.

Let's add `view INDEX`, which looks up the contact in the displayed
list and reports `Showing contact: NAME.`, with the error messages
given in the specification. The command is read-only, so it
overrides `isDataChanging()` to avoid rewriting the data file.

Index parsing mirrors DeleteCommandParser so that both commands
accept the same indexes; extracting a shared parser is left as a
follow-up to avoid conflicts with the delete command's owner.

Showing the expanded contact card is deferred to v1.3.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document view command in User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Users have no guide for the new view command.

Let's add a section describing its format, behavior, examples, and
error messages, in the same style as the delete section, and list
it in the Quick start and Command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add contact presentation requests to command results
commitResults.messageBody:
Command results provide feedback but cannot tell the UI which contact
to select or expand.

Add explicit selection, expansion, and collapse requests with contact
targets. Return these requests from add, view, and list while retaining
the existing result constructors for other commands.

Update command tests to verify the requested presentation and target.
This lets the UI respond without interpreting feedback text.

Refs #63

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement compact and expanded contact cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Contact cards expose the same fields regardless of the user's task,
and command execution does not control selection or expansion.

Show index, role, name, and phone on compact cards. Expand applicable
details on view, select new contacts after add, and collapse on list.
Retain the selected contact when deletion changes its displayed index.

Add role badges, selection highlighting, and wrapping for long text.
Allow a smaller window height and test card rendering, command flows,
invalid input, and selection restoration after simulated rollback.

Refs #63

commitResults.messageTitle: Document contact-card behavior and UI verification
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide describes expanded cards as a future feature, and the
developer guide does not explain the new presentation flow.

Document compact cards, expansion, selection, and deletion behavior.
Explain the command-to-UI contract and provide desktop test commands
and manual checks for resizing, scrolling, and invalid input.

Clarify that restoring model data after a failed save remains the
logic layer's responsibility.

Refs #63
